universities.name: University of Cambridge
universities.funding: STFC Doctoral Landscape Awards provide full funding for Home and some Republic of Ireland and Overseas-fee students; eligible applicants are automatically considered. Some Overseas-fee students also receive Cambridge Trust and Gates Cambridge scholarships, subject to scheme eligibility. DAMTP offers a three-year research PhD; the reviewed page did not confirm specific funding. Not all international applicants are eligible for full funding.

universities.name: University of Oxford
universities.funding: UKRI funding and Oxford scholarships are available for eligible DPhil Astrophysics applicants who apply by the course deadline; award eligibility and extent vary. International-fee eligibility for any particular award was not established by the reviewed pages.
universities.deadlineNote: For 2027-28 entry, the DPhil Astrophysics page lists the deadline as 2027-01-06.

universities.name: Imperial College London
universities.funding: Astrophysics PhD applicants apply through Physics Research (PhD); places are mainly funded by STFC. Imperial states one overseas candidate can be supported by an STFC place. The President’s PhD Scholarship covers full tuition fees and a stipend for 3.5 years; scheme-specific eligibility applies and the pages do not promise full fee coverage to every international applicant.
universities.deadlineNote: October 2026 admissions are closed. As of 2026-10-24, October 2027 project descriptions were forthcoming, expected around early December 2026; no current funded project call was confirmed.

universities.name: University College London
universities.funding: The Astrophysics Group and MSSL offer PhD routes. MSSL describes annual funded places, including STFC studentships covering fees and stipend; non-UK STFC awards are limited. UCL's International Scholar Award for Doctoral Training fully covers overseas fees and stipend for limited non-UK awardees. Other UCL scholarships may cover overseas fees and stipend, but the reviewed pages show current listed rounds closed. Future-round eligibility is unconfirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: The October 2026 MSSL funded-PhD call is closed (STFC deadline 2026-01-19); the Physics & Astronomy group lists 2026-cycle deadline 2026-01-28. No currently open funded call was confirmed.

universities.name: University of Edinburgh
universities.funding: The Institute for Astronomy recruits annually for funded PhD places, including Research Council funding and University scholarships. The institute notes funding limitations may apply to applicants not from the UK or without UK pre-settled status. Full international-fee coverage is not established; confirm eligibility for each award.
universities.deadlineNote: The IfA states applications are closed and will reopen 1 November; the regular-funding deadline of 2026-01-05 has passed. The University programme page gives 2027 funded-position deadline 2027-01-04.

universities.name: Durham University
universities.funding: Astronomy expects several STFC-funded PhD studentships covering course fees and living expenses, typically 3.5 years; international places are limited under UKRI rules. Durham Doctoral Studentships typically include course fees and a 3.5-year stipend and are open to any nationality. A typical Chinese Scholarship Council position is also described as fully funded; nationality eligibility was not expressly confirmed. Scheme and call eligibility must be checked.
universities.deadlineNote: Physics recommends applying by 2026-12-15 for full consideration for available funding; this is a general departmental deadline, not a confirmed funded-project call. The October 2026 astronomy cohort deadline in December 2025 has passed.

universities.name: University of Manchester
universities.funding: The Physics and Astronomy STFC Studentship is stated to be fully funded and open to all nationalities, covering Home or international-rate tuition plus a UKRI-minimum-equivalent stipend for up to 3.5 years. JBCA's 2027 projects are eligible for the general funding pool, but project-specific awards are not guaranteed; eligibility is scheme-dependent.
universities.deadlineNote: For full STFC funding consideration for 2027 projects, submit by 2027-01-22. Other schemes may have different deadlines; the JBCA page advises 2027-01-04 for other listed schemes.

universities.name: University of Portsmouth
universities.funding: The ICG says its 2027 funded PhD cycle is expected to open November/December 2026; dates are anticipatory, not an open call. STFC-funded studentships cover tuition and maintenance, but UKRI caps contributions to international fees at the Home-fee level, so overseas applicants may need to pay a difference. UK and overseas applicants may apply subject to UKRI limits.
universities.deadlineNote: The ICG anticipates a 2027-01-31 deadline for full consideration and 2027-03-31 for self-funded applications; the funded cycle was not open as of 2026-10-24.

universities.name: University of Sussex
universities.funding: Sussex advertises about 10 Astronomy PhD projects annually, with STFC funding typically available to 2-3 students. STFC supports fees and living costs; Sussex says international students may apply, but the reviewed pages do not establish overseas-fee coverage. The STFC scholarship page says applications are closed.
universities.deadlineNote: No current open funded call confirmed. Reviewed project listings were for 2026 admission and are not current open calls as of 2026-10-24.

universities.name: University of Nottingham
universities.funding: Typically 2–3 UKRI STFC-funded places annually; international scholarships encouraged; annual funding information, not a current call.
universities.deadlineNote: Astronomy PhD page gives 31 January 2026 for STFC-funded positions; date has passed. Annual application cycle generally opens November–January.

universities.name: University of Sheffield
universities.funding: Project-dependent funding; official page points applicants to current project listings and scholarships.
universities.deadlineNote: No specific astrophysics/cosmology deadline confirmed on reviewed official page.

universities.name: University of Leicester
universities.funding: Project-specific scholarships/studentships; funding varies.
universities.deadlineNote: No fixed programme deadline stated; January, May and September intakes. Visa-requiring international applicants are advised to apply 5–6 months before start.

universities.name: University of St Andrews
universities.funding: School PhD/EngD scholarships in astrophysics; funded scholarships typically 3.5 years from STFC, University and other sources; current eligibility/availability vary.
universities.deadlineNote: Astronomy STFC and School/University-funded positions: apply by 23 January; later applications may be considered while places remain.

universities.name: University of Glasgow
universities.funding: Most Institute for Gravitational Research postgraduate students are funded by STFC; number varies annually and other scholarships may be available.
universities.deadlineNote: IGR page encourages applications by 11 January for consideration; no year-specific current call confirmed.

universities.name: Cardiff University
universities.deadlineNote: No current official astrophysics/cosmology call with deadline verified; general studentships portal did not expose an official call.

universities.name: Queen Mary University of London
universities.funding: Astronomy Unit funded PhD studentships include STFC (normally up to three per year) and other schemes; international fee coverage may be partial, subject to eligibility.
universities.deadlineNote: Official pages state 28 January 2026 STFC/CSC deadline (passed); next round information was expected in autumn, but a live funded call was not confirmed.

universities.name: University of Warwick
universities.funding: Competitive Warwick Chancellor’s, CSC-Warwick, Pathway, Sanctuary, Warwick-Monash and Bell-Burnell scholarships; STFC route for eligible home-fee applicants. PhD places advertised for October 2027.
universities.deadlineNote: Scholarship expression of interest 16 November 2026; STFC deadline 2 February 2027. STFC projects/site due December 2026.

universities.name: University of Southampton
universities.funding: Range of fully funded PhD studentships; individual project terms/eligibility vary. One current project is fully funded for UK and international candidates.
universities.deadlineNote: Official funded project closes 6 January 2027.

universities.name: University of Leeds
universities.funding: Official Leeds sources list School of Physics and Astronomy Scholarships, STFC Scholarships/Doctoral Training Partnership studentships, Leeds Doctoral Scholarships, China Scholarship Council–University of Leeds Scholarships, Bell Burnell Scholarship Fund, Leeds alumni bursary and self-/externally funded study. The astrophysics group typically offers 1–2 STFC studentships per year, covering UK-rate fees and a stipend for 3.5 years; project-specific eligibility and competition apply. Leeds classifies researchers as home or international for fees; the 2026/27 listed international Physics fee is £32,000 per year versus UK £5,238, and scholarships may cover only UK-rate fees or require separate funding for the international difference. Visa, Immigration Health Surcharge, travel and relocation costs may be excluded.
universities.deadlineNote: No single astrophysics-programme deadline is stated; applications are project-specific. The group page lists ongoing-deadline projects, while the funded STFC project checked here closed on 2026-02-13.

universities.name: University of Birmingham
universities.funding: Advertised PhDs are typically funded by the University or another funding body; the official extragalactic astronomy page states fully funded positions are offered to UK and international students, with an approximately £15,000/year stipend plus some/all tuition. UK tuition is covered in full; overseas students normally must cover approximately £24,000/year tuition, though a small number of overseas-fee waivers or external awards may cover the difference. Self-proposed projects are normally self-funded, with scholarships potentially available.
universities.deadlineNote: For fully funded extragalactic positions, the official page states applications are due 15 January; it does not state the year. For self-proposed research, applications are accepted year-round, with 1 June strongly encouraged for September starts; most funding deadlines are in early spring.

universities.name: Lancaster University
universities.funding: Departmental PhD studentships may cover fees and a tax-free stipend and are funded through UK research councils (including STFC), ERC, Wellcome Trust and other bodies; awards are competitive and subject to academic merit, project and funding availability. Home-fee students have fees aligned to the UK Research Council standard fee/stipend; the 2027/28 international tuition fee is listed as £29,300 full-time (£14,650 part-time), and international applicants should verify whether a studentship covers any international fee-rate difference. International applicants may need separate external funding.
universities.deadlineNote: For the listed Observational Astrophysics PhD projects and consideration for an STFC studentship, the official group page states that applications and references should arrive by 2027-01-31. Lancaster also accepts PhD applications year-round, but funding opportunities are more limited outside the main cycle.

universities.name: University of Hertfordshire
universities.funding: The Centre for Astrophysics Research lists full-time STFC and University of Hertfordshire PhD studentships for October 2026, normally 3.5 years, including fees and a UKRI-rate stipend (£20,780 per year for 2026-27). The page states that both STFC- and UH-funded studentships are open to UK residents and international applicants who meet STFC eligibility requirements; applicants needing a student visa must pay visa and Immigration Health Surcharge costs themselves. Self-funded full-time or part-time PhDs may be considered subject to resources, with fees and living expenses payable by the student. International and UK/EU research-degree fee schedules are separate, so fee status and any difference between the studentship fee coverage and the international fee rate should be confirmed with the university.
universities.deadlineNote: The listed priority deadline for the October 2026 funded round was 2026-02-02 at 09:00 and is past as of 2026-10-24. The general PhD course page lists rolling future start dates, while the CAR page says self-funded applications may be made at any time subject to resources.

universities.name: Liverpool John Moores University
universities.funding: Standard 3.5-year studentships are generally funded by STFC and LJMU research funds; the page states £20,780 per year for PhDs starting in 2026 plus travel and equipment funding. LJMU VC studentships are 100% funded for 3.5 years and open to home and international students. Standard studentships and Bell Burnell scholarships were not open to international (EU and non-EU) applicants for that intake; distance-learning PhDs had no studentships, with stated fees of £15,018 for home students and £26,625 for international students. UK/home versus international fee status should be checked against LJMU’s fee-status rules.
universities.deadlineNote: The official page lists 2026 deadlines: 2026-01-13 for standard studentships and distance-learning fee-only bursaries, 2026-01-30 for VC studentships, and 2026-01-04 internal for Bell Burnell (with the external submission listed as 2026-01-19). These dates have passed as of 2026-10-24; self-funded applications may be submitted at any time according to the page.

universities.name: Trinity College Dublin, The University of Dublin
universities.funding: Astrophysics postgraduate study is available through periodic MSc/PhD positions and School of Physics postgraduate research routes. Trinity's official postgraduate page documents a structured four-year PhD format for some School positions. The astrophysics group page lists funding routes including Irish Research Council/Research Ireland and Trinity scholarships. A Trinity ERC exoplanet listing archived on the postgraduate page offered four years, tuition, a tax-free stipend of €25,000/year, laptop and travel, and was restricted to EU/EEA/UK-based applicants because of differing tuition fees; its nominal start date was 2025-09-01 and it is not treated as a current opening. Research Ireland states the Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship is closed and integrated into the invited-institution Empower programme.
universities.deadlineNote: No current astrophysics-specific PhD call with a verified future deadline was found on an official Trinity page as of 2026-10-24. The Trinity exoplanet positions page describes Research Ireland calls as annual, generally opening in September with October deadlines, but the official Research Ireland page now says the former individual scholarship programme is closed; Empower is an invited institutional call.

universities.name: University College Dublin
universities.funding: UCD School of Physics offers SIRAT research awards for PhD or MSc-by-research applicants; the official 2026 SIRAT call had a 2026-06-25 17:00 deadline and is therefore closed as of 2026-10-24. The School also lists the Thomas Preston PhD Scholarship scheme, but its official page is an old 2022 call. UCD’s graduate-research page states that it welcomes applications for Irish Research Council Government of Ireland postgraduate programmes; Research Ireland’s official page states that scheme is closed and integrated into the Empower programme.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open astrophysics/cosmology-specific UCD call with an unexpired deadline was verified on an official page as of 2026-10-24. The 2026 SIRAT deadline was 2026-06-25.

universities.name: Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies
universities.funding: DIAS has advertised fully funded four-year astrophysics PhD projects covering university fees and a tax-free stipend currently €25,000 per year, with registration at Trinity College Dublin or Maynooth University depending on the project. Research Ireland's open Empower 2026 call includes DIAS among eligible institutions and emphasizes institutional support for PhD studentships and postdoctoral fellowships, but it is an invited institutional call rather than an institution-specific student opening.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open astrophysics, astronomy, or cosmology PhD call was verified on the official DIAS positions page as of 2026-10-24. The listed 2026 DIAS astrophysics PhD calls closed on 2026-03-16 and 2026-04-29.

universities.name: Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics (MPA)
universities.funding: MPA participates in the IMPRS on Astrophysics. Accepted IMPRS applicants hosted at MPA receive a PhD funding agreement equivalent to 65% E13 TVöD Bund, approximately €39,000 gross/year in year 1 and €42,000 gross/year in years 2–3. International applicants are eligible under the IMPRS call.
universities.deadlineNote: IMPRS call for the program starting September 1, 2027: application and recommendation-letter deadline 2026-11-01.

universities.name: Max Planck Institute for extraterrestrial Physics (MPE)
universities.funding: MPE participates in the IMPRS on Astrophysics. PhD funding is through an employment contract or studentship; the official terms state a funding agreement equivalent to 65% E13 TVöD Bund, approximately €39,000 gross/year in year 1 and €42,000 gross/year in years 2–3. International applicants are eligible under the IMPRS call.
universities.deadlineNote: IMPRS September 2027 PhD round: applications and recommendation letters due 2026-11-01.

universities.name: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy (MPIA)
universities.funding: MPIA participates in IMPRS-HD, jointly operated with Heidelberg University. International and German students receive contracts for up to four years to carry out the research required for the doctorate.
universities.deadlineNote: IMPRS-HD application deadline for the academic year starting fall 2027: 2026-11-03 at 14:00 CET.

universities.name: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy (MPIfR)
universities.funding: The IMPRS for Astronomy and Astrophysics offers three-year funded PhD research contracts, competitive salaries, no tuition fees, and workshop, conference, research and travel funding. International applicants are eligible.
universities.deadlineNote: The 2026 application round is open until 2026-10-30 24:00 CET; research contracts can start during 2027.

universities.name: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research
universities.funding: The IMPRS Solar System School fully funds doctoral candidates. MPS states a three-and-a-half-year doctoral support contract at 75% TVöD E13 for IMPRS-funded students, with travel funds and possible wrap-up funding. Other projects may use TVöD contracts or third-party scholarships.
universities.deadlineNote: The published 2026 IMPRS application deadline was 2026-10-01; no clearly open MPS doctoral call was verified on 2026-10-24.

universities.name: Albert Einstein Institute (AEI)
universities.funding: The IMPRS for Gravity at the Extreme is a structured doctoral program funded by the Max Planck Society; students enroll for the PhD at the University of Potsdam or Humboldt University Berlin. International applicants are eligible according to the program's admissions information.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open doctoral position was identified on 2026-10-24; the IMPRS says Potsdam typically has a call in November.

universities.name: Albert Einstein Institute, Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics
universities.funding: The International Max Planck Research School for Gravity at the Extreme provides the structured doctoral route; funding is advertised with available positions. International eligibility and a current stipend amount were not stated on the pages reviewed.
universities.deadlineNote: Hannover PhD positions are advertised as they become available; no current doctoral call was listed on the AEI jobs page on 2026-10-24.

universities.name: Zentrum für Astronomie der Universität Heidelberg (ZAH)
universities.funding: ZAH groups use University doctoral study via the HGSFP and the IMPRS-HD structured astronomy and cosmic-physics program. The HGSFP annual call can provide a fellowship and supervisor/project matching; funding is not uniform across groups. The ESO Studentship Programme is only for people already enrolled in a PhD.
universities.deadlineNote: Current 2027 calls: HGSFP deadline 2026-11-01; IMPRS-HD deadline 2026-11-03 at 14:00 CET.

universities.name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU Munich) — ORIGINS Cluster
universities.funding: LMU participates in the IMPRS on Astrophysics and the DFG-funded ORIGINS Cluster. IMPRS applicants with a five-year Master's degree receive either a PhD employment contract or studentship; LMU/USM funding is approximately 65% E13 TVöD-L equivalent. International applicants are eligible under the IMPRS call. The ESO Studentship Programme is only for people already enrolled in a PhD.
universities.deadlineNote: IMPRS program starting 2027-09-01: application deadline 2026-11-01. LMU Observatory states there are no additional PhD positions outside IMPRS/external funding.

universities.name: Technical University of Munich (TUM)
universities.funding: TUM's Observational Cosmology group supports individual doctoral research. The MPA documents dissertations in cooperation with TUM through individual supervision or the IMPRS on Astrophysics, conducted with MPE, LMU Observatory/USM and ESO. The ESO Studentship Programme is only for people already enrolled in a PhD.

universities.name: European Southern Observatory (ESO)
universities.funding: ESO is a partner in the IMPRS on Astrophysics, which offers about 25 PhD positions in the current call. The ESO Studentship Programme is only for people already enrolled in a university PhD programme; it provides 1–2 year studentships and is not a fully funded 3-year PhD position.
universities.deadlineNote: IMPRS application deadline 2026-11-01. The ESO Studentship Europe call deadline 2026-10-20 had passed by 2026-10-24.

universities.name: Argelander Institute for Astronomy, University of Bonn
universities.funding: AIfA trains international doctoral students through the Bonn-Cologne Graduate School and identifies IMPRS-AA and BCGS routes for PhD fellowships. Funding amounts and guarantees are not specified on the pages reviewed.
universities.deadlineNote: No general doctoral deadline is stated on the institute pages reviewed.

universities.name: University of Hamburg
universities.funding: No general astrophysics PhD funding guarantee is stated. Funding is position- or project-specific. The Quantum Universe Research School (QURS), a structured career-support and training program for doctoral researchers in astrophysics, is available to junior scientists at UHH and DESY; it is not itself a universal studentship or separate degree-awarding route. QURS membership is mandatory for cluster-funded positions.
universities.deadlineNote: The Physics Department's doctoral admission route requires a supervision agreement and research-project outline before the doctoral project begins; doctoral students must enroll after admission. No central PhD application deadline is stated. No funded call demonstrably open on 2026-10-24 was verified.

universities.name: Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam (AIP)
universities.funding: AIP is a non-university research institute and does not award degrees. Doctoral research is conducted at AIP but formally associated with a university, usually the University of Potsdam; the university sets the doctoral regulations and awards the degree. No institute-wide PhD scholarship scheme or general international eligibility terms were verified. AIP says PhD topics are normally tied to available PhD job positions.
universities.deadlineNote: AIP's former Leibniz Graduate School for Quantitative Spectroscopy in Astrophysics was a joint project with the University of Potsdam that started in 2013; its official page describes it in the past tense and was last updated in 2022, with no current intake confirmed. The Astrophysics Network Potsdam is described as a cross-institutional research-and-teaching alliance, not a currently funded doctoral call. AIP's current jobs page, checked 2026-10-24, did not list an astrophysics/cosmology PhD opening.

universities.name: University of Tübingen
universities.funding: Astrophysics PhD funding is project-specific and generally advertised through individual positions; no blanket funding guarantee was verified. The University offers a State Postgraduate Fellowship for eligible final-stage doctoral candidates (2026: up to five months, expected €1,365/month; the 30 June 2026 deadline has passed, and prior individualized funding disqualifies applicants). The Graduate Academy provides general doctoral development and advisory support. International eligibility for the fellowship was not confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: The Faculty of Science offers a Physics doctorate (Dr. rer. nat.) through faculty acceptance and subsequent enrollment. Individual doctorates are available; the Faculty also describes structured doctoral programs generally, but no astrophysics-specific structured program, IMPRS, or MSCA doctoral call was confirmed. No common astrophysics PhD application deadline was found; applications are position-specific.

universities.name: University of Cologne
universities.funding: The University’s doctoral-studies page says physics PhDs are typically conducted through the Bonn-Cologne Graduate School of Physics and Astronomy (BCGS), while applicants generally first find an advisor and discuss project-specific salary and research options with them. BCGS offers mentoring, research internships and travel funds, and limited competitive scholarships for MSc students; its page does not establish a blanket PhD stipend. The DFG-funded Dynaverse Cluster (EXC 3037) identifies BCGS, IMPRS and HDS-LEE as doctoral training networks, not as universal PhD funding guarantees.
universities.deadlineNote: No general PhD application deadline is stated; the Physics Department says most applicants can approach advisors throughout the year, with project-specific conditions. A Labadie-group astrophotonics PhD notice posted 2026-06-15 had a 2026-07-23 deadline and is therefore not open on 2026-10-24.

universities.name: ETH Zurich
universities.funding: Doctoral candidates normally apply within a research group and funding is position-specific; no general astrophysics/cosmology award or universal international eligibility was confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: No central astrophysics/cosmology deadline; group vacancies and the ETH job portal are used.

universities.name: University of Geneva
universities.funding: The Observatory PhD start procedure refers to an employment contract and salary; funding is position-specific and no universal scholarship guarantee was confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: No central astronomy PhD deadline was found.

universities.name: University of Bern
universities.funding: Funding is handled through individual vacancies; the reviewed doctorate page did not specify a general stipend or entitlement.
universities.deadlineNote: No central astrophysics deadline was found.

universities.name: University of Zurich
universities.funding: Theoretical Astrophysics and Cosmology PhD candidates are generally employed and the programme states that salary covers local living expenses; funding depends on appointment.
universities.deadlineNote: No annual programme-wide deadline; current Euclid computational-astrophysics positions accept applications by 2026-11-08.

universities.name: École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
universities.funding: Most doctoral candidates are employed as doctoral assistants; EPFL lists a basic starting salary of CHF 55,225 gross per year from 2026-01-01, while funding remains position-specific.
universities.deadlineNote: The astrophysics laboratory directs applicants to potential advisors and the EDPY Physics doctoral route; no astrophysics-specific funded call was confirmed.

universities.name: University of Vienna
universities.funding: The Vienna International School of Earth and Space Sciences (VISESS) is a structured doctoral programme that includes the Cosmos branch (astronomy, astrophysics and planetology). The official application page says funded praedoc PhD positions are posted year-round, individually or through pooled calls in the University of Vienna job database; funding depends on a specific advertised position and is not guaranteed by programme admission.
universities.deadlineNote: No astrophysics/cosmology PhD or structured-program call with all required details demonstrably open on 2026-10-24 was confirmed on the official pages reviewed; no opening is included. VISESS directs applicants to year-round job postings.

universities.name: University of Innsbruck
universities.funding: Direct route: the University offers a Doctor of Philosophy Programme Physics (6 semesters/180 ECTS), with a dissertation in physics supervised by a team. Structured route: DK-ALM is a collaborative doctoral programme linked to the Institute of Astro- and Particle Physics and lists astrophysics among its topics; its site says FWF funding ran from 2016 to 2025, and its current application page says there are no PhD positions open for external applications (internal applications only), while describing University employment and an approximate gross salary of €39,600/year for successful candidates. The broader PhD page also lists MSCA COFUND DOCC (15 fellows, 3 years; physics among several fields, focused on complex continuum systems). The FWF Special Research Area Dark UNiverse Explorations (DUNE) is an active research network in dark matter, dark energy, cosmology and galaxy formation; no current PhD opening or individual salary funding is asserted here.
universities.deadlineNote: As of 2026-10-24 the Institute for Astro- and Particle Physics official vacancies page states that there are currently no open positions. DK-ALM's official application page says no PhD positions are open for external applications and only internal applications are accepted; no dated open astrophysics/cosmology call with confirmed application deadline was found. No opening record added.

universities.name: University of Graz
universities.funding: No general doctoral funding is specified. The department reports that doctoral positions arise within funded research projects and that candidates may also join with their own funding; this is not a guarantee of a funded place or of eligibility for any specific fellowship.
universities.deadlineNote: The PhD route is the Doctoral Programme in Natural Sciences with Physics Doctoral School supervision; registration entails a synopsis prepared with a supervisor and appointment of a separate school mentor. The university says application deadlines vary by doctoral programme. The Astrophysics and Solar Physics department currently lists no open positions; no funded astrophysics/cosmology PhD call demonstrably open on 2026-10-24 was verified.

universities.name: Leiden University
universities.funding: Leiden Observatory offers paid PhD positions awarded on merit; the current annual call accepts applicants from all countries and requires an MSc by the negotiable start date. University guidance says many PhD candidates are university employees, while others hold their own grants or are external candidates. Astronomy PhD candidates undertake independent research and limited coursework, are enrolled in the Graduate School of Science, and receive astronomy training in agreement with NOVA (Netherlands Research School for Astronomy). Self-obtained grants must cover living costs and a bench fee.
universities.deadlineNote: The current official general call is open with deadline 2026-11-15 for applications and references. Leiden Observatory says the annual call usually closes around November 1, but the current call's explicitly stated deadline governs.

universities.name: University of Amsterdam – Anton Pannekoek Institute for Astronomy (API)
universities.funding: API describes a direct, position-specific route: PhD positions are funded by research grants applied for and awarded to staff, and candidates apply to funded projects rather than entering a general programme and choosing a topic later. PhD researchers are hired as employees, initially for 18 months, with a positive evaluation extending the appointment by 2.5 years for a four-year total. The UvA doctoral programme includes supervisor-agreed research and training plans. A separate API structured cohort was not confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: API states its 2027 recruitment is postponed and expects to publish the job advertisement in December 2026 or January 2027, for projects starting in fall 2027; no API position is currently advertised. The separately listed NWO Mosaic 3.0 national PhD scholarship call has a pre-proposal deadline of 2026-11-03 and is conditional on candidate eligibility and support from an intended supervisor.

universities.name: University of Groningen — Kapteyn Astronomical Institute
universities.funding: Kapteyn is a University of Groningen astronomy department, not a separate degree-granting university. The official UG PhD options page describes employed PhDs as generally four-year employment contracts; the Kapteyn call page describes full-time four-year positions under the Dutch Universities collective labour agreement. This is the primary advertised funded route, with PhD projects attached to specific research grants. The University also describes external-scholarship routes and expressly welcomes international PhD students bringing competitive home-country scholarships, with possible scholarship top-ups. Graduate School of Science is the relevant structured school listed for the Faculty of Science and Engineering. No currently open Dutch national candidate-applied astrophysics/cosmology fellowship was confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open official Kapteyn call verified as of 2026-10-24. The official vacancy page lists a seven-position call whose stated interview period was 2026-01-26 to 2026-02-06 and has passed; its extracted deadline text says 28 November without a year. That call is not included as an opening.

universities.name: Radboud University
universities.funding: Regular PhD candidates are hired on salaried employee contracts with university employment terms; external PhD candidates do not receive a salary and require independent funding. Astrophysics PhD training is attached to the NOVA graduate school. The official pages do not state a universal international-eligibility rule; eligibility is vacancy-specific.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open astrophysics or cosmology PhD call was confirmed on Radboud's official job pages as of 2026-10-24; no applicable deadline is available.

universities.name: Utrecht University
universities.funding: Utrecht states that Dutch PhD candidates are in most cases employed with a salary; the employee route is typically through a vacancy and is governed by the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities. ITP describes a four-year PhD programme with coursework and teaching duties, normally alongside the Dutch Research School for Theoretical Physics (DRSTP). Utrecht also describes scholarship and externally funded routes, subject to admission and a prospective supervisor. DRSTP states that its project leaders obtain research funding from home institutions, NWO, or international sources; this is project-level funding, not confirmation of a currently open candidate-applied fellowship. Utrecht's official pages do not establish a general international-eligibility rule, so none is asserted here.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open astrophysics/cosmology PhD, programme, or fellowship call was verified. The official Utrecht vacancy listing reviewed on 2026-10-24 contained eight positions, none in astrophysics/cosmology; the ITP vacancies page provided general consortium/background information but no currently open relevant call with a confirmed deadline.

universities.name: ASTRON Netherlands Institute for Radio Astronomy
universities.funding: ASTRON describes PhDs as staff-supervised, with doctoral enrolment at one of the Dutch universities in Amsterdam, Groningen, Leiden or Nijmegen; its page directs prospective students to contact astronomy staff about openings. NWO-I identifies ASTRON as one of its institutes and reports PhD researchers among its employees, supporting the Dutch employee-funded appointment model. Doctoral-school affiliation is through the degree-granting university; ASTRON does not document a separate institute-run structured PhD scheme on its PhD page. No separate candidate-applied Dutch national PhD fellowship scheme was verified for this institute. International eligibility for any particular employee-funded position is not confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: No fixed institutional deadline is stated. ASTRON directs prospective PhD students to contact research staff about current openings; no specific officially confirmed open call was verified as of 2026-10-24.

universities.name: SRON Netherlands Institute for Space Research
universities.funding: SRON is an NWO-I research institute rather than a university; no SRON-specific doctoral school or funding scheme was confirmed. Utrecht University’s official guidance describes employed PhD vacancies, often on established projects, with the Dutch Universities Collective Labour Agreement applying, as well as scholarship-funded and externally funded routes. That guidance does not confirm a specific SRON degree-granting affiliation, SRON employment arrangement, or international eligibility; degree registration and funding should be checked per call.
universities.deadlineNote: No official SRON astrophysics/cosmology PhD call or associated deadline was confirmed as open on 2026-10-24.

universities.name: KU Leuven
universities.funding: Direct route: KU Leuven says posted PhD vacancies in principle already have funding via the supervisor; applicants can also contact a professor directly. Structured route: doctoral enrollment and training through the relevant doctoral school, including Arenberg Doctoral School for Science, Engineering and Technology; the doctoral training complements research with thematic and transferable-skills training. Candidate-proposed funding: FWO PhD Fellowship Fundamental Research requires a project prepared with a promotor at a Flemish university and submission by the candidate through the FWO portal. The next confirmed FWO call opens 2026-12-03 and closes 2027-03-01, so it is not yet open on the verification date. F.R.S.-FNRS lists Belgian doctoral schemes, but no KU Leuven-specific eligibility or currently open astrophysics/cosmology call was verified; no FNRS route is asserted here.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open, officially confirmed KU Leuven astrophysics/cosmology PhD call was verified as of 2026-10-24. The Institute of Astronomy vacancy page includes an astronomical-instrumentation PhD advertisement with a 2025-09-21 application deadline, already passed. The next FWO Fundamental Research PhD fellowship call is scheduled to open 2026-12-03 and close 2027-03-01; it is future and not currently open.

universities.name: Ghent University
universities.funding: Direct/professor-led PhD route and funded open-position route: Ghent requires explicit commitment from a professor; an interested candidate may apply to a posted PhD position or approach a professor. PhD enrolment automatically includes the Doctoral School and Doctoral Training Programme, although the programme is mandatory only in some faculties. Funding depends on the position or separately arranged funding. Applicable Flemish funding includes candidate-submitted FWO PhD Fellowships in fundamental research or strategic basic research, prepared with a Flemish-university promotor. Typical annual call timing is winter: the next fundamental-research call opens 2026-12-03 and closes 2027-03-01, so it is not open on 2026-10-24; the 2026 strategic-basic call closed 2026-03-02. F.R.S.-FNRS doctoral funding is not recorded as a Ghent route; its 2026 annual doctoral call listed its own ASP and related instruments and closed 2026-02-17, while the FWO route explicitly covers Flemish-university affiliations.
universities.deadlineNote: No single deadline for the professor-led route; deadlines are position-specific. The next FWO fundamental-research fellowship call opens 2026-12-03 (deadline 2027-03-01), not yet open on the verification date. No relevant current astronomy/cosmology call verified.

universities.name: University of Liège
universities.funding: Doctoral study combines thesis research with doctoral training; ULiège guidance describes an individually prepared project and institutional promoter, followed by validation by the Doctoral College and registration in both the doctoral training programme and doctorate. Potential Belgian schemes include F.R.S.-FNRS ASP (doctoral research fellowship) and FRIA (doctorates linked to industry or agriculture). The FWO fundamental-research PhD fellowship requires affiliation to a university in the Flemish Community, so ULiège is not an eligible host institution under the published rules.
universities.deadlineNote: ULiège states that the 2026–2027 admission application deadline for EU degrees obtained outside Belgium is 2027-06-01; other admission categories' deadline was not confirmed. The next FWO fundamental PhD fellowship call is scheduled to open 2026-12-03, after the verification date. The latest verified F.R.S.-FNRS 2026 doctoral call deadline was 2026-01-15; no 2027 deadline was confirmed.

universities.name: Université libre de Bruxelles
universities.funding: ULB describes doctoral study as structured doctoral training plus original research. Funding routes include part-time research-assistant positions with teaching duties, competitive ULB or third-party fellowships, and recruitment to projects led by ULB researchers. ULB lists F.R.S.-FNRS Aspirant and FRIA among national doctoral funding routes; FRIA is targeted at research linked to industry or agriculture. The FWO fundamental-research fellowship requires affiliation to a university in the Flemish Community, so the official eligibility rule does not provide a ULB-hosted route. No currently open ULB astrophysics/cosmology PhD call was verified.
universities.deadlineNote: No general ULB astrophysics PhD deadline confirmed. F.R.S.-FNRS 2026 Grants & Fellowships doctoral call closed 2026-02-17. FWO fundamental-research PhD fellowship next opens 2026-12-03 and closes 2027-03-01 at 17:00 CET; it is host-restricted to universities in the Flemish Community, not ULB.

universities.name: Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB)
universities.funding: Direct supervisor-led PhD applications; VUB lists funded project positions, employee appointments, and personal fellowships. The FWO fundamental-research fellowship is a candidate-submitted route prepared with a VUB promotor. VUB doctoral candidates automatically enter its flexible Doctoral Training Programme and are affiliated with a Doctoral School.
universities.deadlineNote: The FWO 2027 fundamental-research fellowship call is scheduled to open on 2026-12-03 and close on 2027-03-01 at 17:00 CET; it is not open on the verification date. VUB's general PhD application is by promotor invitation; for registration in the ongoing academic year its published application deadline is 31 May.

universities.name: Institut d astrophysique de Paris (IAP)
universities.funding: Sorbonne Université École doctorale Astronomie & Astrophysique d Île-de-France (ED 127) and EDPIF (ED 564); specific current studentships were not confirmed.

universities.name: Observatoire de Paris-PSL
universities.funding: Doctoral training at Observatoire de Paris with diploma delivered by Université PSL; co-accredited doctoral school and funding from doctoral-school competition, host teams, CNRS, CNES or other sources.
universities.deadlineNote: 2026 doctoral-school competition closed 2026-04-17.

universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed; displayed AAIF dates were for earlier recruitment.

universities.name: Centre de Recherche Astrophysique de Lyon (CRAL), Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1
universities.funding: Lyon 1 ASTRO and COSMO doctoral tracks; LabEx LIO supports doctoral and predoctoral schools. No current CRAL PhD funding call confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.name: Laboratoire d Astrophysique de Marseille (LAM)

universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.funding: IRAP is affiliated with doctoral schools ED 173 SDU2E and ED MITT; official pages report ANR and Horizon 2020 project funding.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.funding: Doctoral training through ED 209 Sciences Physiques et de l Ingénieur; LAB proposes funded thesis subjects and links the University of Bordeaux Infinity² Graduate School.
universities.deadlineNote: No current funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.name: Institut de Planétologie et d Astrophysique de Grenoble (IPAG)
universities.funding: IPAG states PhD students have paid contracts through UGA doctoral schools; official pages cite ANR, ERC, PEPR, CNES and other project funding.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.name: Université Côte d Azur
universities.funding: Université Côte d Azur doctoral schools and OCA-supported astrophysics training; official OCA material documents ANR-supported activity.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.name: Université de Strasbourg
universities.funding: Doctoral training through ED 182 Physique et Chimie-Physique; University-funded projects are published annually and other-funded projects may appear year-round.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.name: Université de Montpellier
universities.funding: Doctorat en Physique through École doctorale I2S; the official doctoral page states thesis monitoring and scholarship allocation are handled by ED I2S.
universities.deadlineNote: No currently open relevant funded PhD call was confirmed.

universities.name: Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC)
universities.funding: The ULL/IAC PhD in Astrophysics is jointly delivered by the University of La Laguna and IAC. IAC states it annually offers up to six predoctoral contracts in Astrophysics and Astrophysics Instrumentation to university graduates worldwide. The currently advertised IAC FPI 2026 call offers three 48-month predoctoral contracts tied to named projects; the call lists annual remuneration of €28,024.68 and a 2026-11-15 deadline. The call states Physics or Mathematics qualification is required for ULL doctoral admission. The call's text has an internal inconsistency: it advertises three vacancies but later says two contracts are offered.
universities.deadlineNote: Current IAC FPI 2026 call deadline: 2026-11-15. No recurring annual deadline verified.

universities.name: Institute of Cosmos Sciences, University of Barcelona (ICCUB)
universities.funding: ICCUB's previous María de Maeztu preselection advertised at least six PhD fellowships, up to four years of predoctoral contract funding, and up to €7,000 for doctoral fees and research mobility; that call had a 2025 deadline and is closed. Selected candidates proceeded to the University of Barcelona's formal selection/admission process. No current astrophysics/cosmology PhD funding call was verified open on 2026-10-24.
universities.deadlineNote: No relevant PhD call verified open today. The live ICCUB ICREA 2027 expression of interest with a 2026-11-01 deadline targets senior researchers, not PhD applicants.

universities.name: Institute of Space Sciences (ICE-CSIC; Institut de Ciències de l’Espai)
universities.funding: ICE-CSIC says PhD theses must be linked to research projects or fellowships and directs applicants to national/regional schemes including FPI (AEI), FPU (Spanish ministry), and FI (Catalan); it says these calls usually open toward year-end. European-project PhD positions are announced on ICE-CSIC's jobs page. PhD candidates enroll through UAB or UB; funding and eligibility depend on each call/project.
universities.deadlineNote: No confirmed PhD-specific opening or deadline on 2026-10-24. ICE-CSIC states national/regional fellowship calls usually open toward year-end.

The UAM doctorate is integrated with its Doctoral School and includes IFT as a participating institution. IFT's 2026 INPhINIT supervisory lines also closed in January 2026.
universities.deadlineNote: No open astrophysics/cosmology funding deadline verified for 2026-10-24. PIX2026 application deadline was 2026-10-05 (closed).

The AEI says applicants should first identify a research group and center and be admitted to a doctoral program, or be able to be admitted by contract signing. IAA's 2025 annual report records Severo Ochoa-funded predocs, but no current IAA-specific Severo Ochoa student call was verified.
universities.deadlineNote: AEI FPU 2026 candidate deadline 2026-11-12; center submission deadline 2026-11-20. No recurring institute-specific cycle verified.

universities.funding: CSIC predoctoral-contract applicants need a qualification granting doctoral access and admission to a Spanish doctoral programme at a university with a CSIC agreement. The AEI FPU 2026 national route is open 2026-10-20 through 2026-11-20; the candidate completes their portion and the host center submits the final application. This does not establish a CAB-specific funded vacancy.
universities.deadlineNote: No CAB galaxy/astrophysics PhD vacancy with a current deadline verified. AEI FPU 2026 host-center submission closes 2026-11-20.

universities.name: Universitat de València / University of Valencia
universities.funding: The Astronomy and Astrophysics Department reports nine active AEI-funded projects. Spain's AEI FPU 2026 doctoral-training call is open nationally: participant forms are due 2026-11-12 and entity submission by 2026-11-20. AEI describes competitive assessment of the applicant's academic record, thesis director, and host research group. No UV- or group-specific FPU slot was confirmed.
universities.deadlineNote: No department-specific PhD vacancy deadline verified. AEI FPU 2026 participant deadline 2026-11-12; entity submission deadline 2026-11-20.

FCT states calls typically occur in March, occasionally March–April.
universities.deadlineNote: No open relevant PhD call verified on 2026-10-24. The FCT 2026 regular doctoral studentship call is closed.

universities.name: University of Lisbon (Ciências ULisboa / IA)
universities.funding: No institution-specific stipend was confirmed. Portuguese FCT doctoral scholarships support eligible candidates enrolled or meeting conditions to enroll in a doctoral cycle. The 2026 general-line call accepted all scientific fields, ran 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-31, and is closed. FCT notes annual call timing is typically March, with occasional variation.
universities.deadlineNote: For 2026/27 PhD admission, period 1 (2026-07-01 to 2026-08-17) is closed; period 2 runs 2026-12-02 to 2027-01-15. The program is four years/240 ECTS.

universities.name: University of Coimbra
universities.funding: Portuguese FCT doctoral research scholarships are available through annual national competitions across scientific fields. universities.deadlineNote: The FCT 2026 doctoral scholarship call closed 2026-03-31. No relevant call verified open on 2026-10-24.

universities.deadlineNote: UiB vacancies are advertised continuously and deadlines are call-specific. Faculty PhD admission has specific rules and deadlines; external-funding candidates apply separately. No active astrophysics/cosmology PhD call was confirmed on an official call page.

openings.title: Theoretical Cosmology, Physics: Quantum Fields, Information, and Next-Generation Cosmological Probes
openings.funding: STFC-funded; full UK-rate tuition fees, annual UKRI-rate stipend (£21,805 for 2026/27), and up to £1,000 per year research expenses; UK-fee-eligible applicants only.

researchWork.description: Theoretical Cosmology, Physics: Quantum Fields, Information, and Next-Generation Cosmological Probes (RS985) Theoretical Cosmology, Physics: Quantum Fields, Information, and Next-Generation Cosmological Probes (RS985) Closing date: 31 October 2026 Key Information Open to: UK fee eligible applicants only Funding Providers: STFC Subject Area: Theoretical Physics Project Start Dates: January 2027 ** **In exceptional circumstances, and subject to the discretion of the University and/or the relevant funding body, a deferral of offer may be granted to the next available enrolment period. Such deferral will typically not exceed a duration of three calendar months from the originally stipulated commencement date. Please note that only one deferral may be considered, and any such deferral is not guaranteed . Supervisors: Azadeh Maleknejad Gianmassimo Tasinato Aligned programme of study: Physics, PhD Mode of study: Full time Place of study: Swansea University (Singleton Campus) Project description: Quantum Fields, Information, and Next-Generation Cosmological Probes This PhD project will investigate theoretical aspects of quantum field theory in cosmological spacetimes, with a particular focus on the physics of the early Universe. It will explore the behaviour of quantum fields in expanding backgrounds, including particle production, the dynamics of cosmological perturbations, and the emergence of effectively classical observables from primordial quantum fluctuations. A central theme of the project will be the role of quantum information concepts in cosmology. Notions such as entanglement, quantum coherence, and information flow offer new perspectives on the quantum-to-classical transition, as well as on the structure and evolution of quantum correlations generated during the early Universe. These questions will be addressed using frameworks from open quantum systems, decoherence, and non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, providing a unified description of quantum fields interacting with a cosmological environment. The project will further aim to connect these theoretical developments with potential observable signatures. In particular, it will investigate how quantum information–theoretic features may be encoded in cosmological and astrophysical observables, and how they could be accessed through next-generation probes, including gravitational-wave observatories, measurements of the cosmic microwave background, and emerging concepts inspired by quantum sensing technologies. The research will be primarily theoretical, relying on analytical methods from quantum field theory, general relativity, and cosmology, with interdisciplinary links to statistical physics and quantum information theory. Eligibility PhD: Applicants for PhD must hold an undergraduate degree at 2.1 level or a master’s degree with a minimum overall grade at ‘Merit’ (or Non-UK equivalent as defined by Swansea University). English Language IELTS 6.5 Overall (with no individual component below 6.0) or Swansea University recognised equivalent. Full details of our English Language policy, including certificate time validity, can be found here. Funding UK fee eligible applicants only Due to funding restrictions, this scholarship is open to applicants eligible to pay tuition fees at the UK rate only, as defined by UKCISA ( Full list of categories for HE in Wales) This scholarship covers the full cost of tuition fees and an annual stipend at UKRI rate (currently £21,805 for 2026/27). researchWork.description: IMPRS HD Application How to apply? How to apply? We encourage an early preparation of the application which will avoid a late arrival after the deadline (that cannot be accepted). The deadline for next term (fall 2027) applications is November 3, 2026, at 14:00 CET. Applications must have arrived by the deadline, including all material and reference letters. Before you do the online application, please read the instructions carefully in order to prepare all material and text in advance. You will find our instructions here. If you notice any mistake after submission, you could simply re-apply, we will consider only your latest application. A complete application must include the following items: A completed web application form , including a list of all courses stating the credits, and grades/marks if no transcripts can be provided. You may also attach a pdf of a course list or the transcripts. Scans of academic certificates including those of the MSc and/or the BSc degree etc. We also need scans of translations of the certificates, if they are not issued in English or German (unofficial translation is enough for the application stage, but for university admission you will need certified translations). For university admission later on - not for the IMPRS application already - also the school leaving exam certificate is needed and all certificates in original form. Note that applicants usually do not have a MSc degree yet, so in this case the BSc and the transcripts are sufficient. If you can provide a grade conversion or a brief explanation of how the grading works in your country, that would support your application. Scans of transcripts and translations (if not in German or English). If already available: A scan of the MSc and/or BSc thesis (with an English abstract if the thesis is not written in English), or published papers. Most applicants will not have a thesis ready at the time of the deadline. The size limit of each pdf is 10MB . Further, two letters of recommendation should be organized (to be uploaded by the referees by the same deadline). Incomplete applications cannot be accepted. How to proceed: A) All applications are ordered and processed by your advert-ID number . Please first register via our application system and obtain that number. For "Reference number of the position advertisement", please enter: IMPRS2027. Also, you must forward the generated ID number to your referees , who will need to upload their letters using that number as well. B) In spite of the personal advert ID, please (1) spell your name in pure ASCII letters (no umlauts, accent, etc), and (2) tell your referees these names. If you have only one name, please use that name as first name and last name. C) Fill out our web application form (activated August 2026). You have to fill it out in one go , so prepare your entries and your uploads in advance. Read our instruction s first. D) Reference letters must be submitted by your referees to the same IMPRS online application system, and must state the same names as in your application. The online system will inform applicants when a reference letter is received. You must tell your referees to submit the letter by the same deadline , tell them also the link to the referee webform . We will never contact your referees.

researchWork.description: the project. When to apply The deadline for the pre-proposal is 3 November 2026, 14:00 CET. Full proposals can be submitted until 4 May 2027, 14:00 CEST. Assessment Criteria The assessment takes place in two phases. Pre-proposals are assessed on the applicant's profile against five criteria, each weighing 20%: prior university education, research experience, motivation for doctoral research, embedding of the research, and training plan. Full proposals are assessed on research design, research approach and methodology (50%), embedding and innovative character (30%), and scientific and/or societal impact (20%). All criteria are scored using the NWO score table, on a scale of 1 (excellent) to 9 (unsatisfactory). To be eligible for funding, a pre-proposal or full proposal must receive an overall qualification of at least 'very good'. Procedure The assessment takes place in two phases. Pre-proposals are assessed by an external, independent assessment committee covering the full breadth of science, which issues positive or negative advice on whether each pre-proposal should be elaborated into a full proposal. The NWO Executive Board decides on this in March 2027. Applicants who may proceed submit their full proposal before 4 May 2027. The proposal is assessed through pre-advice, an interview in September 2027 and an assessment committee meeting. No referees are engaged. The committee advises the Executive Board, which decides on awards in November 2027. Research data management Responsible research data management is an essential component of good research practice. Prepare a data management plan after the grant is awarded and before the project starts. 2 Prepare The assessment takes place in two phases. Pre-proposals are assessed by an external, independent assessment committee covering the full breadth of science, which issues positive or negative advice on whether each pre-proposal should be elaborated into a full proposal. The NWO Executive Board decides on this in March 2027. Applicants who may proceed submit their full proposal before 4 May 2027. The proposal is assessed through pre-advice, an interview in September 2027 and an assessment committee meeting. No referees are engaged. The committee advises the Executive Board, which decides on awards in November 2027. Write proposal The pre-proposal must be written in English and submitted via ISAAC. In it, you describe your academic profile, your key output and your research idea. You also include a statement from the intended promotor or daily supervisor. This phase focuses on your profile, so pay attention to your prior education, research experience, motivation for doctoral research, the supervision arrangements and your training plan. Bear in mind that the assessment committee covers the full breadth of science, so write in a way that is accessible to readers from other disciplines. If the decision is positive, you elaborate the pre-proposal into a full proposal. This sets out your research question, research design and methodology, work plan, scientific and societal contribution, data management and budget. All forms, templates and guidance you need are available on the funding page for this round. [excerpt truncated]

openings.title: PhD fellowship in Astrophysics: Spectral Modelling of UV-optical AGN Emission
openings.funding: Funded salaried full-time PhD employment for up to three years under the Danish state agreement, with benefits and vacation.

researchWork.description: The project The project involves developing software algorithms and pipelines for robust, reproducible, and efficient spectral modelling and analysis of observations from large spectral surveys. The PhD project includes (a) developing modern and efficient software code to perform analysis of AGN spectral data with the aim to robustly perform reliable spectral decomposition of the AGN emission at restframe UV, optical and infrared wavelengths; (b) applying said spectral decomposition algorithm to large databases of AGN Sky Surveys for subsequent analysis; (c) development of algorithms that utilizes Neural Networks to assist in analysis of the large spectral databases of existing and new large sky surveys. Who are we looking for? We are looking for candidates within the field of active galactic nuclei with significant expertise in developing modern software code for spectral modelling of observations of the nuclear UV-optical emission. Candidates with a background in AGN physics, AGN spectral analysis and spectral decomposition are strongly encouraged to apply. Experience in handling large datasets from large Astronomical Sky Surveys, such as Sloan Digital Sky Survey, is a strong asset (i.e., advantage). A background in or experience (whole or in part) with Deep Learning, various neural network architectures and auto-encoders are strong assets. Specific experience with use of high-performance computing, advanced statistics, optimization and performance testing of software algorithms and with scientific software development in Python are all favorable assets. Our group and research- and what do we offer? Vestergaard’s group is part of DARK, Niels Bohr Institute, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. DARK’s areas of research include, but are not limited to, observations, simulations and theory of astrophysical transients and cosmic explosions (including gravitational waves, tidal disruption events and supernovae), neutrino astrophysics, high-redshift galaxies, fundamental cosmology, dark matter, black holes and AGN, and cosmic dust. DARK scientists reside in the new Niels Bohr Building at the North Campus in Copenhagen, sharing space with the other astrophysics sections (Stars & Planetary Sciences, Cosmic DAWN center) and the rest of the Niels Bohr Institute. DARK is committed to excellence through diversity and strives to establish a working climate that welcomes, celebrates, and promotes respect for the contributions of all students and employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to background, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or age. DARK strives to facilitate the progress of underrepresented groups in higher education careers and encourages these candidates to apply. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Included Benefits: 6 weeks of vacation Full social and health benefits (also for partners & family) Generous parental leave For more conditions of employment: http://ism.ku.dk Principal supervisor is Professor M. Vestergaard, DARK, NBI, trn753@ku.dk . The PhD programme We offer the PhD programme as a three-year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme ( 5+3 scheme). This requires an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree. [excerpt truncated]

researchWork.description: Home Information & Events Open Positions Open Positions/Calls Three PhD Positions in Computational Astrophysics The Department of Astrophysics at the University of Zurich invites applications for three PhD positions in computational astrophysics. The positions are part of the Swiss National Science Foundation project “Euclid Science in Switzerland” and are funded for up to four years. ESA’s Euclid space telescope is mapping billions of galaxies across a third of the sky to uncover the nature of dark matter and dark energy. Interpreting these data relies on simulations and theoretical predictions of matching precision, and our group provides them: we develop the N-body code PKDGRAV3 and produced the Euclid Flagship simulations, among the largest cosmological simulations ever performed. The successful candidates will join this effort and work within the international Euclid Consortium, in close collaboration with partners at ETH Zurich, EPFL, FHNW and the University of Geneva. They will be supervised by Dr. Douglas Potter, Prof. Dr. Joachim Stadel and Dr. Aurel Schneider. The scientific computing infrastructure at the University of Zurich is excellent and includes dedicated access to the facilities of the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS). Zurich offers a dynamic and international living environment and is consistently ranked among the world’s best cities for quality of living. Your responsibilities The research covers three broad, overlapping areas: Flagship simulations: Develop and run the next-generation Euclid Flagship simulation with PKDGRAV3 on GPU-accelerated supercomputers. This includes extending the code to identify dark matter halos and their substructure on the fly, and working with our partners to turn the simulation into mock galaxy catalogues for Euclid. Emulators: Build the next generation of the Euclid Emulator: machine-learning models, trained on large suites of simulations, that predict cosmological statistics in milliseconds. The goal is to extend the emulator from the matter distribution to galaxy clustering and lensing statistics. Baryonification and multi-probe cosmology: Model how gas and stars alter the matter distribution predicted by N-body simulations, and develop a pipeline that produces consistent synthetic sky maps (weak lensing, galaxy clustering, X-ray and Sunyaev–Zel’dovich) for Euclid and complementary surveys. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of astrophysics and advanced computational methods. Your profile Applicants are expected to hold a master’s degree (or equivalent) in physics, astronomy or a related field by the starting date. Candidates with a strong interest in high-performance computing, machine learning or numerical astrophysics are especially encouraged to apply. Programming experience is an asset. Further information and application Applications must be submitted through the official UZH job portal: Three PhD Positions in Computational Astrophysics. La solicitud de participación la presenta la entidad incluyendo en ellas a las personas participantes. Some information Leiden Observatory ("Sterrewacht Leiden"), founded in 1633, is the oldest university astronomy department in the world with a distinguished history . The work of famous astronomers such as De Sitter, Hertzsprung, Oort, Blaauw, and Van de Hulst made Leiden an internationally renowned center of astronomical research . We are therefore pleased to announce a general call for several PhD positions with an application deadline of November 15, 2026. Positions are available in several research areas in which the Observatory is active. The research areas of the Observatory include cosmology, galaxy formation and evolution, interstellar matter and star formation, stars and planetary systems, computational astrophysics, high energy astrophysics, laboratory astrophysics, astrochemistry, and instrumentation. The starting dates are negotiable. This year the "Leiden de Sitter Fellowship" , a joint effort with the Leiden Lorentz Institute for theoretical physics is available. This interdisciplinary programme focuses on the interplay between observational cosmology and the physics of the early universe. PhD students in the de Sitter programme will be supervised jointly by members of the physics and astronomy departments, and are invited to (help) propose their own research programme. Savoie Mont Blanc) invites applications for one Master internship followed by a fully funded PhD position in theoretical physics, focused on quantum gravity and cosmological applications. The student will investigate connections between fundamental theory and cosmology, with particular interest in accelerated expansion and the origin of dark energy within string theory and M-theory. The project combines analytical approaches with AI for science, including opportunities to develop new methods and algorithms inspired by physical principles, with applications within and beyond quantum gravity. Qualifications: Applicants should have a strong background in theoretical physics. Internship applicants should be completing a Master's degree in Theoretical Physics or an equivalent programme, and must complete the degree by the PhD starting date. Applicants for the PhD only should hold, or expect to obtain by September 2027, a Master's degree in Theoretical Physics or equivalent. Basic programming skills and familiarity with AI and machine learning are welcome but not required. The emphasis is on a solid physics foundation and an interest in learning new methods during the project. Knowledge of French is not required. Research Environment and Supervision: The student will join the Mathematical Physics group at LAPTh, supervised by Dr. G. Bruno De Luca. A postdoctoral researcher will be recruited at the same time and will work closely with the student, contributing to a growing research team. The project is funded by the Multidisciplinary Institute for Artificial Intelligence (MIAI), offering opportunities for interaction with researchers in fundamental physics, mathematics and AI. The position provides dedicated computing resources, support for conferences and research visits, and a vibrant research environment with strong regional and international connections. The laboratory is located in Annecy, in the French Alps, about 45km from Geneva. Its proximity to CERN offers further opportunities for scientific exchange and collaboration. Terms of Employment: The Master internship is funded and will last up to six months, starting in Spring 2027. It will be followed by a three-year PhD starting in September 2027, with some flexibility possible. PhD funding is already secured, under a standard Univ. Savoie Mont Blanc doctoral contract with the usual salary and social benefits. Continuation from the internship to the PhD is expected automatically, subject to satisfactory performance.

openings.title: Why do galaxies stop forming stars, and why do they end up with bulges?
openings.funding: Fully funded (UK and international)

researchWork.description: Why do galaxies stop forming stars, and why do they end up with bulges? Funding Fully funded (UK and international) Type of degree Doctor of Philosophy Entry requirements 2:1 honours degree 2:1 honours degree View full entry requirements Faculty graduate school Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences Closing date 6 Jan 2027 On this page About the project Potential supervisors Entry requirements Fees and funding How to apply Contact us About the project Potential supervisors Entry requirements Fees and funding How to apply Contact us About the project In this project you'll build transparent, data-driven models that switch quenching ingredients on and off, one at a time, and test them against new data from the Euclid space telescope, the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Rubin-LSST telescope to reveal what really shuts galaxies down. Galaxies come broadly in two main flavours: blue, star-forming discs and red, quenched systems with a prominent central bulge. The drivers behind such a dichotomy are still a matter of intense debate. This project aims to tackle this fundamental mystery in astronomy making use of flexible and transparent, data-driven numerical models that connect observations directly to theory. You'll build and extend semi-empirical models in which galaxies grow along their host dark matter halo merger trees at the rate imposed by observed star formation rates, and central supermassive black holes grow following observed Eddington-ratio distributions and duty cycles. With such flexible tools, you'll be able to test one ingredient at a time: does quenching happen when a black hole reaches a threshold mass, or when the halo becomes massive enough, or after mergers and disc instabilities? which recipe best reproduces quenched fractions, galaxy scaling relations and bulge-to-total ratios? Because every assumption is explicit and can be switched on or off, these models show clearly what the data demand and what they do not. Your predictions will be tested against new data from Euclid, JWST and Rubin-LSST, covering millions of galaxies, and compared with outputs from simulations such as TNG and EAGLE. If you have a creative and curious mind, this is the project for you. The School of Physics and Astronomy is committed to promoting equality, diversity inclusivity as demonstrated by our Athena SWAN award. We welcome all applicants regardless of their gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation or age, and will give full consideration to applicants seeking flexible working patterns and those who have taken a career break. The University has a generous maternity policy, onsite childcare facilities, and offers a range of benefits to help ensure employees’ well-being and work-life balance. The University of Southampton is committed to sustainability and has been awarded the Platinum EcoAward. What is the mechanism for energy extraction in black holes, 10 times more efficient than nuclear fusion. Accreting black holes are the most luminous steady stellar sources in the Galaxy when they actively swallowing matter. Their extreme powers are generated in their accretion discs, and they feed back huge energies to their surroundings through superfast winds and relativistic streams of jet plasmas. In this PhD, you will exploit state-of-the-art multiwavelength observations from frontline facilities to carry out comprehensive novel studies of the immediate environments of Galactic black holes. You will: use timing and spectral observations in X-rays to measure the physical conditions responsible for feedback changes with accreting of matter using NASA's JWST complemented by a suite of radio, optical and X-ray datasets test some of the leading theories regarding the formation and evolution of discs and jets. The aim is to test and refine models of the immediate accreting environments around black holes, which can help to test the growth of black holes across cosmic time. You will learn: coding for data data analysis and scientific inference, including computer simulations use of world-leading astronomical facilities, especially JWST and multiwavelength fast-timing detectors critical thinking, presentation, and publication skills. There will be opportunities to develop worldwide collaborations, especially in Japan, USA and South Africa.
